correctness.rationale: For each fixed environment the ordered increment pair is a bounded two-dimensional martingale with cross-bracket equal to the time average of the predictable signs. Inclusion-induced cardinality ties give the exact conditional-mean product indexed by odd binomial coefficients. Lucas parity provides 2^popcount(m) active independent factors. The binomial maximum-atom bound and count of low-popcount integers imply the L2 norm of the environmental mean tends to zero uniformly over nondegenerate parameter arrays. Independent rows are independent L2(driving signs)-valued elements; convergence of the weighted Hilbert martingale and Kronecker lemma give quenched L2 Cesaro vanishing almost surely. Boundedness upgrades the bracket to compact-time convergence in conditional probability and verifies martingale FCLT hypotheses. The standalone exact-rational verifier checked 131841 parity identities and 45 heterogeneous expectation identities plus five analytic bound comparisons. It does not purport to certify the limit.

value.rationale: The primary 2026 article explicitly leaves the quenched counterpart of its independent time-by-cardinality model open; proving it for all uniformly nondegenerate heterogeneous Bernoulli arrays advances a defined mathematical question about when averaged random bootstrap behavior holds for almost every coefficient environment. The exact Boolean parity/binary-popcount mechanism overcomes strong within-size correlation and the Hilbert-law-of-large-numbers step makes the conditional conclusion possible. It provides a structural result about an infinite random-process family, not a finite calculation or a routine rephrasing of an existing theorem.
